Change Trigger (User Story V1 → V2): US-001 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 1): As a user, I want to create an item that is correctly associated with my account. | Register a new user; authenticate with that user's credentials; create an item with a title and description. Expected behavior: HTTP 200; returned title and description match the request; an item id is present; owner_id matches the registered user.

US-002 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 2): As a superuser, I want to read an item by ID. | Authenticate as the superuser; create an item; retrieve that item by its returned id. Expected behavior: HTTP 200; returned title, description, id, and owner_id match the created item.

US-003 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 3): As a user, I want the API to report when an item does not exist. | Authenticate as the superuser; request an item using an id that does not exist. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

US-004 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 4): As a user, I want item ownership to prevent other users from reading my items. | Register two normal users; user A creates an item; user B attempts to retrieve user A's item. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Not enough permissions'.

US-005 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 5): As a superuser, I want to list items. | Authenticate as the superuser; create two items; request the item list. Expected behavior: HTTP 200 and the returned collection contains at least both newly created items.

US-006 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 6): As a superuser, I want to update an item. | Authenticate as the superuser; create an item; update its title and description. Expected behavior: HTTP 200; title and description are updated while id and owner_id remain those of the original item.

US-007 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 7): As a user, I want the API to report when an item being updated does not exist. | Authenticate as the superuser; attempt to update an item using a nonexistent id. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

US-008 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 8): As a user, I want item ownership to prevent other users from updating my items. | Register two normal users; user A creates an item; user B attempts to update user A's item. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Not enough permissions'.

US-009 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 9): As a superuser, I want to delete an item. | Authenticate as the superuser; create an item; delete that item. Expected behavior: HTTP 200 with message 'Item deleted successfully'.

US-010 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 10): As a user, I want the API to report when an item being deleted does not exist. | Authenticate as the superuser; attempt to delete an item using a nonexistent id. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

US-011 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 11): As a user, I want item ownership to prevent other users from deleting my items. | Register two normal users; user A creates an item; user B attempts to delete user A's item. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Not enough permissions'.

US-012 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 12): As a user, I want to obtain access token. | Authenticate using the configured superuser credentials. Expected behavior: HTTP 200; access_token is present and non-empty; token_type is 'bearer'.

US-013 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 13): As a user, I want login attempts with an incorrect password to be rejected. | Register a user; attempt to log in with the correct email and an incorrect password. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 and authentication fails.

US-014 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 14): As a user, I want to validate access token. | Authenticate as the superuser; call the access-token test endpoint with the returned token. Expected behavior: HTTP 200 and the response identifies the superuser email as admin@example.com.

US-015 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 15): As a user, I want to send password recovery email. | Register a normal user; request password recovery for that email; inspect the mail-catcher service. Expected behavior: HTTP 200 with message 'Password recovery email sent', and a recovery email is captured by the mail service.

US-016 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 16): As a user, I want password recovery for nonexistent accounts to be rejected. | Request password recovery for an email that is not registered. Expected behavior: HTTP 404.

US-017 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 17): As a user, I want to reset password with recovery token. | Create a user; authenticate as superuser; obtain the user's password-recovery HTML/token; submit a reset request with a new password. Expected behavior: HTTP 200 with message 'Password updated successfully'.

US-018 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 18): As a user, I want password resets with invalid tokens to be rejected. | Authenticate as the superuser; submit a password-reset request using an invalid reset token. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Invalid token'.

US-019 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 19): As a user, I want to create and retrieve a user by ID. | Create a user through the private user-creation operation; authenticate as superuser; retrieve the created user by its returned id. Expected behavior: Creation and retrieval return HTTP 200; retrieved email and full_name match the created user.

US-020 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 20): As a user, I want to read superuser profile. | Authenticate as the superuser; retrieve the current-user profile. Expected behavior: Response body is non-empty; is_active is true; is_superuser is true; email matches the configured superuser.

US-021 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 21): As a user, I want to read normal user profile. | Register and authenticate a normal user; retrieve the current-user profile. Expected behavior: Response body is non-empty; is_active is true; is_superuser is false; email matches the registered user.

US-022 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 22): As a superuser, I want to create a user. | Authenticate as the superuser; create a new user with a generated email and password. Expected behavior: Successful 2xx response; returned email matches; id is present; is_active is true.

US-023 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 23): As a superuser, I want to retrieve a user by ID. | Register a normal user; authenticate as superuser; retrieve that user by id. Expected behavior: Successful 2xx response; returned email and id match the registered user and is_active is true.

US-024 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 24): As a user, I want to retrieve own user by ID. | Register a normal user; log in; retrieve that user's record by its id using the user's token. Expected behavior: Successful 2xx response; returned email and id match the authenticated user.

US-025 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 25): As a user, I want normal users to be prevented from reading other users by ID. | Register and authenticate a normal user; request a different/random user id. Expected behavior: HTTP 403 with detail indicating the user does not have enough privileges.

US-026 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 26): As a user, I want the system to reject duplicate user creation. | Authenticate as superuser; create a user; attempt to create another user using the same email and password. Expected behavior: Second creation returns HTTP 400 and does not return an _id field.

US-027 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 27): As a user, I want normal users to be prevented from creating other users. | Register and authenticate a normal user; attempt to call the privileged create-user operation. Expected behavior: HTTP 403.

US-028 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 28): As a superuser, I want to list users. | Authenticate as superuser; create two distinct users; retrieve the user list. Expected behavior: HTTP 200; response contains data and count; both newly created users appear in the data collection.

US-029 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 29): As a user, I want to update own profile. | Register and authenticate a normal user; update the current user's email and full name. Expected behavior: HTTP 200; returned email and full_name equal the submitted new values.

US-030 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 30): As a user, I want to change and restore password. | Authenticate as superuser; change the current password to a new password; verify login with the new password; restore the original password and log in again. Expected behavior: Both password updates return HTTP 200 with success message; login succeeds with the active password after each change.

US-031 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 31): As a user, I want the system to reject wrong current password. | Authenticate as superuser; attempt to change the password while supplying an incorrect current password. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'Incorrect password'.

US-032 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 32): As a user, I want duplicate profile emails to be rejected. | Register two users; authenticate as the first; attempt to change the first user's email to the second user's email. Expected behavior: HTTP 409 with detail 'User with this email already exists'.

US-033 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 33): As a user, I want password changes to require a genuinely new password. | Authenticate as superuser; request a password change where current_password and new_password are the same valid password. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail 'New password cannot be the same as the current one'.

US-034 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 34): As a user, I want to register valid user and login. | Generate valid email, password, and full name; register the user; then log in with the generated credentials. Expected behavior: Registration returns HTTP 200 with matching email and full_name; subsequent login succeeds.

US-035 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 35): As a user, I want registration with an existing email to be rejected. | Attempt to register a new account using the already configured superuser email. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 with detail stating that a user with the email already exists.

US-036 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 36): As a superuser, I want to update a user by ID. | Register a normal user; authenticate as superuser; update that user's full_name by id; retrieve the user again. Expected behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 with the new full_name, and the value remains changed when the user is re-fetched.

US-037 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 37): As a user, I want to update nonexistent user. | Authenticate as superuser; attempt to update a user identified by a generated UUID that does not exist. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 with detail indicating that the user id does not exist.

US-038 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 38): As a user, I want updates that reuse another account's email to be rejected. | Register two users; authenticate as superuser; attempt to change the first user's email to the second user's email. Expected behavior: HTTP 409 with detail 'User with this email already exists'.

US-039 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 39): As a user, I want to delete own account. | Register and authenticate a normal user; delete the current user's account; then attempt to log in again. Expected behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 with message 'User deleted successfully'; login with the deleted credentials fails.

US-040 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 40): As a superuser, I want the system to prevent me from deleting my own privileged account. | Authenticate as the configured superuser; attempt to delete the current user's own account. Expected behavior: HTTP 403 with detail 'Super users are not allowed to delete themselves'.

US-041 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 41): As a user, I want to delete a user by ID. | Register a normal user; authenticate as superuser; delete the registered user by id; attempt to log in as the deleted user. Expected behavior: Delete returns HTTP 200 with success message; login for the deleted user fails with HTTP 400.

US-042 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 42): As a superuser, I want deletion of nonexistent users to return a clear not-found response. | Authenticate as superuser; attempt to delete a user using a random UUID that does not exist. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 with detail 'User not found'.

US-043 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 43): As a superuser, I want the system to prevent deletion of my own account by ID. | Authenticate as superuser; obtain the current superuser id; attempt to delete that same id. Expected behavior: HTTP 403 with detail 'Super users are not allowed to delete themselves'.

US-044 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 44): As a user, I want normal users to be prevented from deleting other users. | Register two normal users; authenticate as user A; attempt to delete user B by id; verify user B can still log in. Expected behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 403 with insufficient-privileges detail, and user B remains active.

US-045 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 45): As a user, I want to cascade item deletion after admin deletes user. | Register a normal user; create an item as that user; authenticate as superuser and delete the user; then retrieve the item by id. Expected behavior: User deletion returns HTTP 200; the former user's item is no longer available and retrieval returns HTTP 404.

US-046 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 46): As a user, I want to cascade item deletion after self-delete. | Register a normal user; create an item; delete the user's own account; authenticate as superuser and request the former item. Expected behavior: Self-deletion returns HTTP 200; the former user's item retrieval returns HTTP 404.

US-047 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 47): As a user, I want registration passwords shorter than the minimum length to be rejected. | Attempt to register a new user with a password exactly 7 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-048 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 48): As a user, I want registration passwords longer than the maximum length to be rejected. | Attempt to register a new user with a password exactly 129 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-049 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 49): As a user, I want excessively long full names to be rejected. | Attempt to register a new user with a full_name exactly 256 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-050 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 50): As a user, I want new passwords shorter than the minimum length to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to update the password with new_password exactly 7 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-051 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 51): As a user, I want new passwords longer than the maximum length to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to update the password with new_password exactly 129 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-052 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 52): As a user, I want invalid current-password field lengths to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; submit a password-update request with current_password exactly 7 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-053 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 53): As a user, I want item creation with an empty title to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to create an item with an empty title. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-054 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 54): As a user, I want excessively long item titles to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to create an item with a title exactly 256 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-055 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 55): As a user, I want excessively long item descriptions to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to create an item with a description exactly 256 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-056 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 56): As a user, I want password resets with too-short new passwords to be rejected. | Submit a password-reset request with new_password exactly 7 characters long. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error before token validation.

US-057 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 57): As a user, I want malformed registration email addresses to be rejected. | Attempt to register a user with a malformed email address. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-058 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 58): As a user, I want malformed profile email addresses to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to update the current profile to a malformed email address. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-059 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 59): As a user, I want malformed user identifiers to be rejected. | Authenticate as superuser; request a user using a non-UUID identifier. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-060 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 60): As a user, I want malformed item identifiers to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; request an item using a non-UUID identifier. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-061 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 61): As a user, I want null registration emails to be rejected. | Attempt to register a user with email set to null. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-062 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 62): As a user, I want null registration passwords to be rejected. | Attempt to register a user with password set to null. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-063 (RESTestBench fastapi requirement 63): As a user, I want null item titles to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to create an item with title set to null. Expected behavior: HTTP 422 validation error.

US-064 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 1): As a user, I want to create and retrieve a user. | Create a user with username, email, and password; obtain the returned token; retrieve the current user with that token. Expected behavior: Creation returns HTTP 201 with matching username/email and a token; current-user retrieval returns HTTP 200 with the same account data.

US-065 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 2): As a user, I want follow relationships to be updated correctly and self-following to be prevented. | Create two users; have user A follow user B; retrieve B's profile as A; then have A attempt to follow itself. Expected behavior: Following B returns HTTP 200 and following=true; the profile remains marked followed; self-follow is rejected with HTTP 400.

US-066 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 3): As a user, I want to create an article and resolve slug. | Create and authenticate a user; create an article with title, description, body, and tags; retrieve it using the returned slug. Expected behavior: Creation returns HTTP 201; fields and tags are preserved; slug starts with the normalized title; retrieval by slug returns HTTP 200 with the article.

US-067 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 4): As a user, I want to update an article while preserving slug. | Create a user and article; update the article title and description using the original slug; retrieve it again by that slug. Expected behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 with new values, and retrieval via the original slug returns the updated article.

US-068 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 5): As a user, I want deleted articles to become unavailable. | Create a user and article; confirm the article can be retrieved; delete it by slug; attempt retrieval again. Expected behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 and the article is no longer retrievable successfully.

US-069 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 6): As a user, I want my feed to contain articles only from users I follow. | Create a reader and two authors; each author creates an article; check the reader's feed before following anyone; follow one author and check the feed again. Expected behavior: Initial feed contains no articles; after following one author, the feed contains that author's article and excludes the unfollowed author's article.

US-070 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 7): As a user, I want to add and retrieve article comment. | Create a user and article; add a comment to the article; retrieve the article comments. Expected behavior: Comment creation returns HTTP 200; the comment is retrievable with the expected body and has a numeric id.

US-071 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 8): As a user, I want to delete an article comment. | Create a user, article, and comment; delete the comment by id; retrieve the article's comments again. Expected behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 and the deleted comment is absent from the comments collection.

US-072 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 9): As a user, I want duplicate usernames and email addresses to be rejected. | Create a user; attempt another registration with the same username but different email; then another with different username but the same email. Expected behavior: Both duplicate attempts return HTTP 400 with a uniqueness error.

US-073 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 10): As a user, I want unfollowing to update relationship state and self-unfollowing to be prevented. | Create two users; have user A follow user B; then unfollow B and retrieve B's profile; finally attempt to unfollow A itself. Expected behavior: Unfollow returns HTTP 200 and following=false; profile remains unfollowed; self-unfollow is rejected with HTTP 400.

US-074 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 11): As a user, I want login to verify passwords correctly. | Create a user; log in once with the correct password and once with an incorrect password. Expected behavior: Correct login returns HTTP 201 with matching user data and a valid token; wrong-password login returns HTTP 401.

US-075 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 12): As a user, I want to filter articles by tag. | Create a user and three articles with overlapping and distinct tags; query articles by several tag values. Expected behavior: Each tag filter returns only matching articles; a nonexistent tag yields zero matching articles.

US-076 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 13): As a user, I want to filter articles by author. | Create two authors and one article per author; query articles separately by each author and once without an author filter. Expected behavior: Each author query returns only that author's article; the unfiltered query contains both articles.

US-077 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 14): As a user, I want to update my profile bio and image. | Create and authenticate a user; update bio and image through the current-user endpoint; retrieve the user again. Expected behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 with the submitted bio/image and a later retrieval shows the values persisted.

US-078 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 15): As a user, I want to paginate the article list using limit and offset. | Create five articles; request the article list with limit=2, then limit=2 with offset=2, then a limit larger than the dataset. Expected behavior: Pagination respects limit and offset; total count remains 5; the large-limit request returns all five articles.

US-079 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 16): As a user, I want profiles to reflect the current follow relationship. | Create two users; inspect target profile before following; follow the target and inspect again; unfollow and inspect a third time. Expected behavior: following changes false -> true -> false while the target username remains correct.

US-080 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 17): As a user, I want articles to be associated with the correct author. | Create two users; each creates one article; request articles filtered by each username. Expected behavior: Each author filter returns exactly the article created by that author and excludes the other author's article.

US-081 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 18): As a user, I want article tag lists to be stored and retrieved accurately. | Create one article with three tags and another with an empty tag list; retrieve both by slug. Expected behavior: The first article returns exactly the three stored tags as an array; the second returns an empty tag array.

US-082 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 19): As a user, I want an article's updated timestamp to change when the article is modified. | Create an article and record created/updated timestamps; wait briefly; update the article; retrieve it again. Expected behavior: created remains unchanged and updated becomes newer than its original value.

US-083 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 20): As a user, I want articles with the same title to receive unique slugs. | Create two articles with the same title under the same user and capture both generated slugs. Expected behavior: Both creations succeed; slugs share the normalized title prefix but are different because of their suffixes.

US-084 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 21): As a user, I want article titles and descriptions to persist correctly. | Create an article with a known title and description; retrieve it by slug. Expected behavior: Retrieved title and description exactly match the values supplied at creation.

US-085 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 22): As a user, I want public profiles to return the correct bio and image. | Create a user; set a known bio and image; retrieve the public profile by username. Expected behavior: Profile returns the correct username, bio, and image.

US-086 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 23): As a user, I want to paginate my followed-user article feed. | Create reader and author; reader follows author; author creates five articles; request feed with limit=2 and then limit=2&offset=2. Expected behavior: Feed reports total count 5 while returning two items per page; the offset request returns a different page.

US-087 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 24): As a user, I want articles ordered from newest to oldest. | Create three articles separated by short delays; retrieve the global article list. Expected behavior: Articles are ordered by creation timestamp descending, with newest articles first.

US-088 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 25): As a user, I want JWT tokens to contain the correct user identity. | Create a user; decode the payload of the returned JWT; also use the token to retrieve the current user. Expected behavior: JWT payload contains the correct user id, username, and email; authenticated user retrieval matches the same account.

US-089 (RESTestBench nestjs-realworld requirement 26): As a user, I want multiple article comments to be stored with unique IDs. | Create a user and article; add three comments with distinct bodies; retrieve all comments for the article. Expected behavior: Three comments are returned; each has a unique id and each original comment body is preserved.

US-090 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 1): As a user, I want my todo list to contain only my own todos. | Register two users; each creates a different todo; user A requests GET /todos. Expected behavior: The returned list contains user A's todo and does not expose user B's todo.

US-091 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 2): As a user, I want todos without a title to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to create a todo with an empty or missing title. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 Bad Request with validation-error details.

US-092 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 3): As a user, I want to read a todo by ID. | Register and authenticate a user; create a todo; retrieve it using the returned id. Expected behavior: The response contains the correct todo data for the created id.

US-093 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 4): As a user, I want nonexistent todos to return a not-found response. | Register and authenticate a user; request a todo id that does not exist. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 Not Found.

US-094 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 5): As a user, I want other users to be unable to access my todos. | Register users A and B; user A creates a todo; user B requests user A's todo id. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 and user B cannot access user A's todo.

US-095 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 6): As a user, I want to delete a todo from database. | Register and authenticate a user; create a todo; delete it by id; request the same id again. Expected behavior: Deletion returns HTTP 200 and subsequent retrieval returns HTTP 404.

US-096 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 7): As a user, I want deletion of nonexistent todos to return a not-found response. | Register and authenticate a user; attempt to delete a todo id that does not exist. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 Not Found.

US-097 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 8): As a user, I want other users to be unable to delete my todos. | Register users A and B; user A creates a todo; user B attempts to delete that id; user A retrieves it afterward. Expected behavior: User B receives HTTP 404 and user A's todo still exists.

US-098 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 9): As a user, I want to update a todo completion status. | Register and authenticate a user; create an incomplete todo; update isComplete to true; retrieve it again. Expected behavior: Update returns HTTP 200 and the retrieved todo has isComplete=true.

US-099 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 10): As a user, I want todo updates with mismatched route and body IDs to be rejected. | Register and authenticate a user; create a todo with id X; call PUT /todos/X using a body whose id is Y. Expected behavior: HTTP 400 Bad Request.

US-100 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 11): As a user, I want updates to nonexistent todos to return a not-found response. | Register and authenticate a user; submit a valid update for a todo id that does not exist. Expected behavior: HTTP 404 Not Found.

US-101 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 12): As a user, I want other users to be unable to update my todos. | Register users A and B; user A creates a todo; user B attempts to update it; user A retrieves it afterward. Expected behavior: User B receives HTTP 404 and user A's todo remains unchanged.

US-102 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 13): As a user, I want to register user with valid credentials. | Register a new user with a valid email and password. Expected behavior: HTTP 200 and registration succeeds.

US-103 (RESTestBench todoapp requirement 14): As a user, I want todo access to require authentication. | Request GET /todos without an Authorization header or token. Expected behavior: HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
